source.title: Introduce Flink-Kafka Transactions Management Tool
source.search_operation: site:github.com/apache/flink Kafka producer fenced checkpoint failover restart transactionalId issue PR; site:issues.apache.org/jira FLINK Kafka producer fenced checkpoint failover transactional.id

observation: The issue states that when a Flink job using KafkaSink with EXACTLY_ONCE stops unexpectedly, it can leave Kafka transactions in ONGOING state. Those lingering transactions block downstream read_committed consumers because the Last Stable Offset cannot advance. The issue states there is currently no built-in way to resolve this without restarting the original Flink job or waiting for transaction timeout. Its proposed transaction-management CLI would abort by reconnecting with the same transactional.id to fence the previous producer, or commit by resuming the exact producerId and epoch recovered from Flink checkpoint state/logs.
failure_mechanism: Unexpected execution loss can leave an externally authoritative Kafka transaction neither committed nor aborted. A local/scheduled-chat success or durable checkpoint is therefore not sufficient to establish downstream business completion: the broker-side transaction obligation remains authoritative. The ticket's proposed remediation is an operator-run CLI, so that remediation itself is a residual external/manual execution dependency under the current Phase-1 acceptance rule.
falsifying_trace: The Flink job stops unexpectedly while a Kafka transaction is ONGOING.
The transaction remains ONGOING at the broker and read_committed consumers cannot advance beyond it.
Without restarting the original job or waiting for transaction timeout, current Flink has no built-in resolver according to FLINK-39218.
The proposed alternative invokes a separate CLI that fences the prior producer or resumes the exact transaction, which requires an external execution step.
exact_scope_guard: Evidence is limited to the Flink KafkaSink EXACTLY_ONCE unexpected-stop/lingering-transaction scenario described by FLINK-39218 and to the remediation design described there. It does not establish that every Flink failure leaves an ongoing transaction, that every Kafka exactly-once integration has this failure, or that a merged future version lacks an integrated recovery path.

phase1_assessment.reason: The proposed recovery tool is a separate CLI/operator execution path; the issue also names restart/wait as current alternatives.
phase1_assessment.incremental_monetary_cost: 0 for this evidence-gathering run; acceptance of the proposed CLI route is rejected for residual execution dependency rather than cost

exact_next_action: On a fresh bootstrap, verify exactly one non-duplicate source family for whether any merged/current Flink KafkaSink path automatically reconciles broker-side lingering EXACTLY_ONCE transactions after crash without operator CLI, manual restart, wait-for-timeout, hosted compute, finite quota, or added cost. Preserve scope; do not rerun FLINK-39218 as the sole operation.
